name: Azrikam
overview: Azrikam was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified specifically as the son of Neariah. His mention is brief and focused in the genealogical record found in 1 Chronicles 3:23, with no additional notes or narrative details provided.
namesAndTitles: The name Azrikam means '[my] help arises,' reflecting a Hebrew proper name with a theistic implication. This name is not indicated as given directly by God but carries a sense of divine assistance or support as understood in its original language context.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Azrikam was the son of Neariah, establishing a clear father-son relationship. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented for Azrikam in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Azrikam's significance lies primarily in his place within the genealogical lineage of Judah, as recorded in 1 Chronicles. His inclusion in this record underscores the continuity of the tribe of Judah, which is central to the biblical narrative and God's covenantal promises. Though not elaborated upon in narrative form, his mention helps preserve the historical and spiritual heritage leading to Christ.
